claim: To stop a plotter painting the screen, replace its store instructions with same-length ones (NOP, or CP (HL) to keep 7 T and the access) so state and timing stay identical to the original.
limit: Not safe when the removed paint was a write the game later reads (Starquake): save and restore those bytes.

evidence.text: Removing only the plotter's stores kept every register and all timing equal at each frame boundary, bar A and F inside the plot and blit loops that follow the bytes read.
Paint site LD (HL),D became CP (HL) not NOP: 7 T and one cell access; the NOP was 3 T a cell faster. Build stayed in lockstep for 600 rounds.
A routine whose store is a read instead of a write takes the same time to the T-state.
Replacing a store with NOP keeps instruction counts and the lockstep; a watch at the site still checks the store's would-be effect.
Only screen pixel and attribute write instructions were removed; the plotters keep running so all game state stays the original's.
NOPing the painter dropped a write the game reads: the paint ran past the attribute area into 0x5B00, read by collision.
